items.detail: Mono, or stereo downmixed to mono by the per-frame mean and recorded; PCM16 or IEEE float32 at 48 kHz, written back byte-exact. Truncated chunks, size overflow, non-finite samples, unsupported formats and files past the frame bound are refused. Held by test pcm16_roundtrip_is_byte_exact in crates/patchback-audio/tests/wav.rs.
items.label: WAV input and output without an audio crate

items.detail: Identifiers, port rates, parameter contracts, the ports of each kind, cycles and provisional resource caps are checked, in the order the specification declares; a refusal names its error and the node, edge or line. Only a validated patch compiles, into a deterministic execution plan (ready nodes by lowest identifier, one buffer per output port). patchback patch validate runs the checks and the compilation on a .patch file. Held by test accepted_the_default_voice_validates_and_compiles in crates/patchback-core/tests/patch_graph_validation.rs.
items.label: A typed patch graph, validated before it runs

items.detail: A versioned, human-readable patch file in physical units, parsed into a loaded, unvalidated patch and written in canonical form; write then parse is bit-exact. Unknown versions, duplicate keys or IDs, malformed numbers, unsupported rates, lines outside the grammar and lengths past the provisional bounds are refused with the line, and nothing is loaded. patchback patch validate reads it. Held by test default_voice_write_then_parse_is_identity in crates/patchback-core/tests/patch_file_format.rs.
items.label: The line-oriented .patch file

items.detail: Eight parameters, each with an index, a stable path, a normalized-to-physical mapping and its inverse, a physical range and a default; the defaults are placeholders until the design sets them. An out-of-range normalized value is clamped and the clamp recorded; a non-finite value and an invalid contract are refused. Held by test subtractive_mono_declares_the_eight_contracts_in_design_order in crates/patchback-core/tests/parameter_contracts.rs.
items.label: Parameter contracts for the subtractive voice

items.detail: A versioned, line-oriented list of sample-timestamped note events, parsed into a note sequence and written in canonical form; write then parse is bit-exact and sample offsets are exact. Notes that do not end after they start, overlap in a monophonic sequence or fall outside the MIDI or velocity range, unknown versions, duplicate keys, malformed numbers, lines outside the grammar and lengths past the provisional bounds are refused with the line, and nothing is loaded. Notes only; patchback render refuses a sequence whose rate is not the rendering rate. Held by test write_then_parse_is_identity_over_generated_sequences in crates/patchback-core/tests/note_events.rs.
items.label: Note events and the notes.events file

items.detail: One monophonic voice at 48 kHz: a polyBLEP saw oscillator, a bounded tanh drive, a TPT state-variable lowpass with cutoff clamped below Nyquist and resonance to its contract range, a linear ADSR with sample-accurate note-on, retrigger and note-off and safe zero times, a smoothed VCA and output gain, and a protective limiter whose engagement is counted and reported. Golden waveform, envelope and filter tests hold the units; high-note aliasing against a naive saw is measured. Held by test the_adsr_matches_its_golden_segments in crates/patchback-dsp/tests/units.rs.
items.label: The fixed subtractive voice

items.detail: patchback render --patch --notes --out [--block-size]: a compiled patch plays a note sequence into a mono 48 kHz float32 WAV lasting to the last note's end plus the release and a provisional 100 ms tail. The same inputs give the same bytes at every block size; bounded controls give finite samples. Whether the limiter engaged and how many samples it changed are printed. An unsupported rate, a block size of zero or less, a patch or note sequence that does not load, an uncompiled patch, a render past the length bound and a non-finite sample are refused and nothing is written. Held by test render_writes_a_float32_wav_with_the_default_block_size_and_with_512 in crates/patchback-cli/tests/render.rs.
items.label: Deterministic offline rendering

items.detail: patchback analyze --input --out: radix-2 FFT, Hann-windowed STFT at 512, 2048 and 8192 samples, RMS and peak envelopes, spectral centroid, rolloff, flatness, log-band energies, spectral flux and f0 estimation, written to one versioned analysis file. Silent input, an ambiguous or out-of-range pitch, a clip too short for the f0 search, non-finite samples and sizes past the provisional bounds are refused and nothing is written. Held by test analyze_writes_one_versioned_analysis_file in crates/patchback-cli/tests/analyze.rs.
items.label: Native FFT, STFT and audio descriptors

items.detail: patchback compare --reference --candidate: the candidate is aligned to the reference by up to 100 ms, then log-spectral (512, 2048 and 8192 samples), envelope, transient and band-energy terms, each in [0, 1] and 0 for identical clips, are printed with the design's weights, their weighted sum and the lag. Clips at different rates and lengths alignment cannot absorb are refused. The tolerance, spectral floor and term definitions are provisional. Held by test compare_prints_the_loss_and_its_components in crates/patchback-cli/tests/compare.rs.
items.label: A multi-resolution audio comparison

items.detail: patchback fit --input --notes --out: from the default patch, then from seeded restart points, coordinate search over the eight normalized parameters (step 0.25, halving) renders and scores each candidate against the reference and keeps only a strictly lower valid loss. It stops at the render budget (--max-renders), the wall-time bound (--max-wall-time-ms), the restart count (--max-restarts) or when a restart improves less than --improvement-threshold, and writes the best patch as patch.patch with the run's other files. The same seed and inputs give the same patch. Invalid bounds, a missing reference or note sequence, a silent or unpitched reference and a run without a valid candidate are refused and nothing is written. The defaults and the smallest step are provisional. Held by test fit_writes_the_best_patch_and_reports_the_run in crates/patchback-cli/tests/fit.rs.
items.label: Bounded derivative-free search

items.detail: patchback fit writes patch.patch, notes.events, reconstructed.wav, report.txt, run.meta and trace.events into the output directory. reconstructed.wav is the clip the best patch was scored on, so patchback compare of the reference and it prints the best loss again; report.txt holds the losses, counts, stop reason, wall time and warnings; run.meta the seed, the input digests, the ModelSpec pin, the feature contract and the bounds; trace.events one line per evaluation. Any of the six already present is refused before the search, and a failed write removes everything the run wrote. The same seed and inputs write the same files, report.txt's wall time aside, unless the wall-time bound stops the run. Held by test the_same_seed_and_inputs_write_the_same_patch_in_two_processes in crates/patchback-cli/tests/fit.rs.
items.label: The fit run's six files

items.detail: patchback benchmark synthesizes a seeded holdout of reference clips with known notes, scores the default patch on each and fits each from it, and records the lower median loss of both, the reduction, whether the 20 % go/no-go target was met, the median render evaluations, the wall time and three listening examples in benchmark.txt, clips.txt and examples/. Both verdicts complete the benchmark. The same flags write the same files, benchmark.txt's wall time aside. Held by test a_small_benchmark_completes_and_its_files_agree in crates/patchback-cli/tests/benchmark.rs.
items.label: A baseline against the default patch

items.detail: An external recording is imported only with its provenance and licence recorded beside the clip; one missing either is refused and no clip exists. A clip imported as synthesized by Patchback needs neither and records its origin and, when given, its render. The two checks come before the file is read: a recording missing either is refused even when the file is missing, truncated or corrupt. The patchback commands take no origin, provenance or licence yet. Held by test external_recording_with_provenance_and_licence_imports_and_keeps_both in crates/patchback-audio/tests/provenance.rs.
items.label: Provenance for every fixture

items.detail: An audit of the resolved Cargo.lock passes a workspace with no third-party application crate but clap, the one reviewed CLI parser, and its reviewed closure; it refuses a forbidden or unreviewed crate and any ModelSpec crate, and admits at most one approved audio I/O backend with its reviewed closure, only behind an optional feature. Held by test the_application_crates_take_no_third_party_crate_but_clap_and_its_closure in crates/patchback-cli/tests/dependencies.rs.
items.label: A dependency gate

items.detail: ModelSpec 0.5.0 is pinned in models/modelspec.pin by version, commit and binary checksum; CI installs that binary and runs modelspec check on models/patch_regressor.mspec. A binary reporting another version is refused, and a model the pinned binary rejects is recorded as rejected and cannot be trained. Held by test a_rejected_source_cannot_be_trained in crates/patchback-model/tests/adapter.rs.
items.label: A pinned ModelSpec that checks the model

items.detail: 32 values per note: eight band energies over attack, body and release windows, then RMS, peak, spectral centroid, rolloff, flatness, zero-crossing rate, attack-envelope slope and normalized MIDI pitch. A contract is defined once per version, amended only as a draft and frozen by publishing; extraction runs only under a published contract, and a value that cannot be computed reliably or is not finite is refused rather than estimated. Held by test feature_contract_extract in crates/patchback-analysis/tests/features.rs.
items.label: The frozen feature contract features/1

items.detail: patchback generate-dataset writes normalization.stats: the mean and population standard deviation of each features/1 value over the training split's rows, computed in f64 under the dataset's published contract. Statistics from the validation or test split, under an unknown or draft contract, or under a version the contract does not carry are refused. The same statistics normalize features at training and inference, as (x − mean) / std, with divisor 1 for a feature whose training values are all equal; features of another contract version and non-finite values are refused. The x.f32 of every split, validation and test included, holds the features z-scored under the training statistics. Held by test normalization_stats_train_only in crates/patchback-dataset/tests/normalization_scenarios.rs.
items.label: Training-split normalization statistics

items.detail: patchback generate-dataset draws patch seeds from SplitMix64 of --seed. From each seed's own xoshiro256** stream it draws eight normalized parameters, a MIDI note from 36 to 84 and a gate from 0.25 to 1.5 s, log-uniform. It renders each draw with the same DSP engine and extracts features/1, then fills train, validation and test to exact multiples of the batch size 16. Splits are isolated by patch seed. Clipped, silent and noisy renders go to a separate diagnostic set and never into a split. Each split is written as ModelSpec dense data: x.f32 (N × 32) of features z-scored under the training split's statistics and y.f32 (N × 8), row-major little-endian f32, and order.u32 (the row indices). Each file is read back and checked: its byte count, finite values in x.f32 and y.f32, and each row index once in order.u32. The same seed writes byte-identical dataset.meta, samples.meta and dense files. Held by test a_real_generation_fills_each_split_with_valid_isolated_samples in crates/patchback-dataset/tests/generate.rs.
items.label: A deterministic paired dataset

items.detail: A fixed-shape two-layer MLP, 32 features to 8 normalized parameters, checked and trained by modelspec on its CPU backend. patchback_model::TrainingRun runs modelspec train --backend cpu on a written training split, with an optional evaluation split, under a timeout; exit status 0 completes the run, and its stdout gives the loss curve and the evaluation loss. On generated data the pinned ModelSpec 0.5.0 lowers the loss from 1.0717294 to 0.8882302 in 4 steps on 64 rows. The run is a library call with no patchback command yet; patchback_model::WeightArtifact::export writes its checked weights to a checksummed weights/1 file. Held by test the_pinned_modelspec_trains_on_real_generated_data in crates/patchback-model/tests/pinned_training.rs.
items.label: A parameter regressor trained with ModelSpec

items.detail: patchback_model::WeightArtifact::export reads the stdout of a completed run of the pinned ModelSpec and refuses any line outside its documented init, step, eval and param lines, a parameter other than @PatchRegressor.w1 and .w2, shapes other than [32, 64] and [64, 8], counts other than 2,048 and 512, and non-finite values. It writes a new weights/1 file: a header with the model, the ModelSpec version and commit, the feature contract and the payload's SHA-256, then 10,240 bytes of little-endian f32. WeightArtifact::read verifies the header, the length and the checksum. On the pinned ModelSpec 0.5.0 all 2,560 values read back as printed. A library call with no patchback command yet. Held by test the_weights_of_a_pinned_run_are_exported_and_read_back in crates/patchback-model/tests/pinned_export.rs.
items.label: Checked weight export

items.detail: The exported weights are run by a small Rust matmul and ReLU predictor held to golden tests. Milestone B.
items.label: A native predictor

items.detail: The search starts from the regressor's prediction instead of the default patch, benchmarked against the default patch and the raw prediction. Milestone B.
items.label: A regressor-seeded fit

items.detail: Onsets, pitches, gate lengths and tails of external audio, each with a confidence; an ambiguous estimate is refused with a diagnostic. Milestone C.
items.label: Monophonic note estimation with confidence

items.detail: One editable patch and its event sequence for an isolated bass or lead phrase. Milestone C.
items.label: Short phrases

items.detail: Saw, square and sine oscillators, filter families, LFO and delay; the topology is chosen by rendering and ranking candidates, with a simplicity penalty. Milestone D.
items.label: Candidate topologies

items.detail: Time-varying control events, and cycles only through an explicit delay of at least one sample. Milestone D.
items.label: Control automation and delayed feedback

items.detail: Several monophonic or polyphonic stems, drum and effect modules, repeated-pattern analysis and arrangement events. Milestone E.
items.label: Stems, drums and arrangement

items.detail: Supported training moves to ModelSpec's GPU backend once it ships and passes CPU/GPU equivalence tests. Milestone E.
items.label: GPU training through ModelSpec

items.detail: One card per module kind with its ports (direction, rate, meaning) and parameter contracts (index, path, mapping, physical range, default). The prototype renders illustrative fixture data. Patch studio.
items.label: Module catalogue view

items.detail: A validated patch drawn as nodes by rank and edges coloured by port rate, with delayed feedback routed as a z⁻¹ return path through a Delay node. Patch studio.
items.label: Patch graph view

items.detail: A finished fit run replayed evaluation by evaluation: loss curve, retained or candidate patch, parameter trajectories and topology changes. Replays a fixture trace until a fit run writes one. Patch studio.
items.label: Fit evolution replay

items.detail: The same view following a running fit, frames streamed over server-sent events from a std-only Rust server on 127.0.0.1. Patch studio.
items.label: Fit evolution live

items.detail: The retained patch, its parameters against the reference, and reference and render spectra at an FFT length of 512, 2048 or 8192. Patch studio.
items.label: End result view
